author: FX.Sniffer
text:
MCFly wrote: I'm not sure I like the explaination in the vids about why the gaps tend to get closed but in the end they mostly do.

Everyone points at S/D, Balance and Imbalance in a different way without explaining the real mechanics behind it.

Although in my previous posts I tried to make it clear why LQ gap gets filled but I’ll repeat it in a simple phrase;

In LTF LQ gaps gets filled because - When pro money enter with their big orders it moves the price away and against their entry price, therefore they await for price to return to their entry price to continue adding their orders.

In HTF LQ gaps get filled because – When pro money closes their buy orders they become sellers, and when they close their sell orders they become buyers.

Thank you.

author: MCFly
text:
Hi FXSniffer,

I made a little mistake. I have posted the short nobrainer vid but there was a longer one and it seems it is no longer available on youtube. I was refering to the longer vid. In this vid nobrainer said that when the big pockets of demand/supply come in the market makers are not able to hedge or cover their risk at any given point of time because of missing liquidity on the bid/ask side. Now at some point "somebody" is stepping in to close the gaps in order to help to stabilize price.

So what he says is that gap filling is covering naked exposure. I don't think that's the whole story. I'm sharing your opinion.

So what he says is that gap filling is covering naked exposure. I don't think that's the whole story. I'm sharing your opinion.

Makes sense McFly, institutional market makers/dealers are the specialists, they are in the same rank as pro money, in fact they deal directly with individual and institutional pro money, they are an informed traders due to their big informed clients. They have to act quickly and silently in hedging their client's orders before anyone else notice. In worst cases in order to keep their client they can take big losses over a long time of period due to their capital but they know how to return their losses with a bit of profit.

Cheers,

Some analysis on Gold;

Starting with the weekly TF, price is residing below a key level preceded by a bearish engulf, if we combine the engulf with the one next to it on the left we'll get an inverted bearish pb with close below KL. The this week could a retest of KL or a change in decision but or me taking into consideration the break of engulf's low is a sign bearish move.

Note: we can clearly see a strong selling with momentum from the top swing high to the present area.

Next is H4 TF, and potential zones and S/R flips from the same TF. on the far right side price broke through the S/R and into the DBD which has a stacked DP from LTF, a successful retest of the broken S/R will push the price higher to the KL and lower edge of the large broken demand (now supply) where it should drop from there. A break through the next higher S/R could change the whole scenario.

A failure retest of current S/R breaking it south is also a change in scenario and an end of retracement.

Finally M30 TF, same levels from previous TF and a clearer view of the stacked supply zones. So now it's up to PA to guide us.
